exposure: mode of delivery (caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 20 healthy full-term infants aged 1-6 months, delivered via either caesarean section or vaginal delivery.
finding: The early stage of intestinal bacterial colonisation was altered in the caesarean section group compared with the vaginal delivery group, with specific differences in the abundance of Pseudomonadota, Enterobacteriaceae, and Bacillota phyla/families.
mod_finding: Caesarean section delivery was associated with altered early-stage intestinal bacterial colonisation in infants compared to vaginal delivery, specifically showing higher abundance of Pseudomonadota and Enterobacteriaceae, and lower abundance of Bacillota in the CS group.
